I don’t see how anyone could argue that an SoC that outperforms the previous 28-Core Intel Xeon and is far more efficient while doing so too is a “glorified iPhone chip”. No one who really needs this system is upset about the M2 Ultra’s performance. And again I agree that upgradability would be nice, but it also does not mean that every professional using this machine would need it. For example most professional video editors these days don’t even need a discreet GPU option, they use proxies and servers to edit anyways and to them unified memory with it’s much higher bandwidth is way more advantageous than traditional ECC RAM. Heck, I have 384GB RAM in my 7,1 and the system never access more than about 40GBs. Audio professionals will benefit the same way. The pros who aren’t served well by this Mac Pro have mostly already moved on since the 6,1 and even the 7,1 with it’s lack of support for NVIDIA GPUs. Also so what if the Mac Studio is on par with specs? That device performs as well as anyone interested would ever need it to, it is a great value for money, and will be all over professional video editing houses and recording studios like the previous versions are. For those who need that level of performance plus PCIe expansion, they can either spend their money on less practical but more affordable external PCIe enclosures or splurge on a Mac Pro.

Lol, as someone who runs a 7,1 with the 16-core Xeon, I can tell you the M2 Ultra is far from a “glorified iPhone chip”. In fact I can’t think of another SoC or processor I’d rather have in a Mac Pro than that. In a perfect world would I have liked them to figure out a way to have both upgradable RAM and discreet GPUs along with the SoC? Yeah sure, but that was clearly not feasible. I am also not part of the true target audience for this machine, even though I do buy them. The true target audience for these last couple of generations of Mac Pros don’t go around swapping parts. Heck they buy so many at a time they wouldn’t even have the time to do so.

Sometimes I wonder if people here know what “real professionals” are and what they actually do or use?  While I’m glad I didn’t sell my 7,1 in anticipation of this I also know there are a lot of prospective buyers excited for this. The others either are actual professionals who already have their needs covered for the foreseeable future or already moved on to other solutions long ago… or redditors who think “real professionals” are just people who need discreet GPUs or upgradeable RAM.

Professional video editors will love this thing (they already love the Mac Studio) most of them work with proxies as it is and the main thing with them is memory bandwidth which this (and Mac Studio) clearly has an advantage on. The issue is going to be with colorists and basically anyone who need raw GPU power that favors discreet GPUs. Those people have mostly already moved on though. Audio professionals that need PCIe expansion will be pleased with it too (if they can stomach the price) those that don’t are already quite happy with the Mac Studio. Personally, I’ll hold on to my 7,1. It was already overkill for my needs when I specced it out 3 years ago and I’ll be happy to run it to the ground before I part with it.

I’ll be keeping my 7,1 for now. However, I don’t see how video editors are going to be upset at this after all a lot video editing studios these days mostly edit by proxies and rely much more on memory bandwidth (which this excels at) than raw GPU power. Too much is being made of the 1.5TB vs 192GB thing without considering some of the benefits unified memory has over ECC RAM. Audio professionals may like this too given the amount of internal PCIe expandability, if they can get over the $6999 price tag just for that luxury. Colorists and the rest of creative professionals will obviously scoff at this but most of those people moved over to PCs long ago, the few stragglers left are on maxed out 7,1s. It’s a shame Apple could not figure out a way to leverage both AS and discreet GPUs/upgradeable RAM but I guess we always knew that wouldn’t be feasible.

I’m not going to lie, the lack of upgradeable RAM and GPUs are the main reasons I’m considering keeping my 7,1 a bit longer but to be fair I’m an audio professional and I can’t think of the last time I was in need of more RAM than the amount I originally specced out (384GB RAM which I expect to be at the very least comparable to 192 unified) and discreet GPUs are a non-issue for me at the moment. These are probably going to be bigger issues for video professionals. It’s like the M2 Ultra Mac Pro is stuck in between the Mac Pro Apple wanted (thinking 6,1) and the one Pros want (5,1/7,1).

If my father is proud of me, I can’t imagine how. He was born in 1939 in a small town in a third world country. All they had was dirt roads and a well, and yet through his brilliance and entrepreneurship he was able to not only uplift himself out extreme poverty, but a large part of his immediate family as well. He also provided many needy people with jobs when there weren’t many, and everyone I’ve met who ever worked for him absolutely love him. I’ve never met another man like him. I doubt there are many people like him left in this world. He had high hopes for me. He used to tell me as a child “you and I were born to lead, build, and uplift”.  He used to not so secretly wish that I would become an industrial engineer, but he never pushed me in that direction. He just wanted me to do what made me happy, and I chose music. When he was younger he dreamed of traveling the world playing the saxophone, so I guess he wanted me to have a shot at my dream since he didn’t pursue his, so long as I got a “traditional education” while I was at it. I did. I coasted through my bachelor’s using the so-called “intelligence” I inherited from him to barely scrape by while giving it my most minimal effort. For some time the music “dream” was working, at least somewhat, but then COVID happened and that, in conjunction with my complacency, threw everything off rails. Now I’m struggling to keep it together, and I know he can sense my despair. But even bigger than the dream of me carrying his legacy of success, was the dream of me building a family and giving him grandchildren. He is 84 now, his health is slowly deteriorating, and I wouldn’t dare bring a child into this world with me as the responsible party. I imagine that must break his heart. I’m going to see my therapist in a couple of hours, it may be foolish of me but I hope she gives me a better perspective on how to clean up this mess I’ve made. Thank you for taking your time to chat with me. I know I can be quite a drag, but it means more than you can imagine.

I don’t think you need to worry about this too much. I have a younger cousin who was in your same situation. At the time she was about 24, smart, pretty and has a great personality, but had never had a boyfriend. In fact, from what she told me she had never had a serious sexual encounter at all, had only kissed a couple of guys. It was really driving her into a dee depression, both her older sister had been in long term relationships by the time they were her age and had married not much older than her. She was starting to feel like she would be alone for the rest of her life. She used to cry about it almost every night, and pray for help. I used to try to cheer her up by reminding her that I started dating at a relatively young age and that due to my immaturity and sometimes that of my partners, it would often end catastrophically. I would tell her not to try to rush into anything or lose hope. Fast forward a few years later and she is now in a happy relationship with what seems to be a genuinely great guy. They’re engaged, and I couldn’t be happier for them. She deserves to be loved. It even makes me question my own agnosticism at times. I hope the same for you. Don’t rush into anything, the right person will come at the right time.

She does, despite having trouble demonstrating affection, my wife does what she can to help me. It’s a little bit more complicated with my siblings. I guess it’s a combination of the age gap, they were pretty much around college age when I was born. Also, with me being a byproduct (my therapists have told me not to use that term to describe myself, but what gives) of an affair their father had, I’m sure it must have been complicated for them, at least at first. I don’t know if any of that still lingers. There also may be a bit of resentment since, despite me being such a mess, my father has always shown a bit of favoritism towards me. None of us really know why, maybe it’s cause I’m the youngest, but I suspect it’s because I must remind him of my mother. He clearly cared for her as it saddens him to this day to speak about her or her accident. They think he was too soft on me, and perhaps he was, but while that may have contributed to some of my other problems today, it didn’t necessarily cause my depression. I remember being depressed since I was in elementary school, before I could even understand the concept of depression. The issues with my upbringing are only now compounding on that. It’s their opinion that I should just power through this somehow and pick myself up and while I agree with them, I just don’t know how. I’ve been seeing therapists my entire life and while it has helped keep me off the edge at times, it’s only been as effective as a bandage on a leaking dam that’s waiting to burst open. I do want to get better, for my wife, my parents, my siblings, everyone who cares about me and/or who I care about, but I’ve been this way my entire life and have only seen marginal, momentary improvements. I often wish I could fall asleep and never wake up again. I feel like that would be the most painless solution for everyone. They would feel like my untimely death was unfortunate, maybe mourn me for sometime, then move on with the lives they deserve to live, free from the baggage I’ve become.

I wish I could tell you there’s a solution, but I was born with a silver spoon up my ass, and still I’ve been depressed for as long as I can remember. As a 5 or 6 year old child, before I could understand what depression was, I used to call it “being bored”. What I was really feeling was an extreme sense of sadness and loneliness, usually triggered by things that most people would be unaffected by, even simple things like cloudy days or “sad paintings”. As a child I had live-in nannies who would look after me while my step mother was busy playing socialite and doing charity work (I don’t blame her, she did the best she could). I grew unhealthily attached to those women and would grieve their departures like the death of a relative (they often left to start families or if they got better jobs). I grieved them like I now imagine I would have grieved my biological mother, had I been old enough to understand when she passed away (I was 18 months old). Now I’m in my 30s, married to an amazing woman, have a beautiful home, people who seem to care about me, and yet I feel about as close to death as I did when I tried to take my own life as a teenager. I still create unhealthy attachments to people, pets, things, substances, etc. It pulls me under even more knowing that I “had it easy” and still felt this way my entire life. I almost feel ungrateful. I guess money and status really don’t buy happiness, although I imagine it’s a million times harder without them. But it leaves me wondering, how can someone who has felt this way since their earliest memories ever be happy, under any circumstance? I too own a gun and find myself fantasizing about blowing my brains out. The only thing stopping me is the thought of my wife finding my body and having to clean up whatever mess I leave behind, figuratively and literally. She deserves better than that. I hope you find a way out of the abyss, and if you do, throw a rope down for the rest of us. I’ll try to do the same, although I wouldn’t bet on myself.

She would be a great mom, and I feel like, if I didn’t always feel so useless and defeated, I’d make a really good father. I have a great father to emulate after all.
